Arachne Story III is strange:

If what is written is literally what it is, she had very mundane modern origin and is placed at her position because she want that role.

And before Arachne become what she is, there are practically no need for anyone to weave the fate.
Practically she made her own prison by doing the weaving.

Ehh it’s partially yes and no, because while she did take the initiative to claim her role as “weaver of fate” the fact that the Moirae wheel found itself in her hands as a gift was also a form of “fate”, and she herself knew that, and felt dutybound to pick it up

But that also means, fate itslef is flowing naturally without her intervention or role.
There are just no requirement or need of herself to be prisoner and burdened by that role

The last part is honestly more inference than direct information, but it’s based off of how she treated the tasks afterwards, and her actions of assigning Rea (the Leng Spider Maid) to keep her continuing the task
I mean yeah, all Arachne really does is adjust things & cut them off from what we’ve seen, so it’s not implausible that there was a previous weaver who was doing the same before her

And like I said above, the required role of “prisoner” was self-imposed, and honestly more from Nefraea’s standpoint than Arachne’s, because while the 2.5 PV does have her calling herself that, we also do know that ||Nef is/was originally part of Arachne, and was split off and later shunned to the “Abyssal Prison|| so it makes sense that she views it as both a duty and her shackles, in a way

The whole of chapter 5 is really just essentially ||Nefraea trying to get Arachne to give up on that duty, to throw her responsibilities away, not because Nef wants the power, but because she’s that part of Arachne that once shunned the deeds she had to do, and Arachne denying that option and choosing to continue forward||
